title: Green completes the Lausitzring double as Audi take the top five
dek: Jamie Green won Sunday's 46-lap race from pole by 2.144 seconds, passing Mattias Ekström on lap 8 after being beaten at the start, as Audi filled the top five places.

chapters.title: Saturday's one-two-three-four
text: Saturday had ended with an Audi one-two-three-four. Jamie Green passed pole-sitter Miguel Molina on lap 25 of 32 and won Race 1 by 4.261 seconds, Edoardo Mortara and Mattias Ekström followed him past the fading Molina, and the Spaniard ended up fourth. The win put Green top of the standings on 50 points, ahead of Mortara on 48 and Ekström on 40, and Audi had now won every race of 2015.

Ballast was not adjusted between the two races of a weekend, so the performance weights of Saturday applied again on Sunday. The race was the longer of the two, an hour plus one lap, with a compulsory tyre change, and BMW and Mercedes needed a response after a Saturday in which one BMW and three Mercedes had made the top ten.

chapters.title: Green on pole by half a second
text: Green answered his Saturday second place with a statement: 1m17.386s in the 20-minute session, 0.520 seconds clear of Ekström, who held second ahead of Timo Scheider's Phoenix Audi by 0.025 seconds, with Molina another 0.009 seconds back in fourth. It was Audi's fourth pole in four qualifying sessions this year, and this time the championship leader was the one in front. Green said the lap had simply been good, though he expected a hard hour.

The first Audi chaser was Maxime Martin's BMW in fifth, 0.568 seconds off the pole time, and he said Audi was too fast for his car. Mortara was sixth, Augusto Farfus seventh for BMW Team RBM, Nico Müller eighth and Rockenfeller ninth, so Audi held seven of the first nine places. Daniel Juncadella's Mercedes was tenth, 0.670 seconds behind Green and the best-placed Mercedes.

There were casualties further back. Gary Paffett qualified 11th, Bruno Spengler 13th and Paul di Resta only 22nd, while Martin Tomczyk was 23rd. Reigning champion Marco Wittmann qualified 17th, 0.855 seconds off pole, and Timo Glock 21st. Spengler started the race from 18th on the grid, and Maximilian Götz set no time and started last.

chapters.title: Ekström leads away, Green fights back
text: Green had pole but not the start. Ekström got away better from second on the grid and led into the first corner. Green tried to take the lead at Turn 1, ran wide on the exit and had to wait, but a lap later he fired down the inside. That happened on lap 8, roughly ten minutes into the race, and Green then pulled out an advantage.

The first lap had cost others dearly. Wittmann made a good start and was pressing, but touched Wickens at Turn 6 and was forced off into the gravel at Turn 7, and he rejoined well behind the pack. Blomqvist and Paffett were out within four laps. Wehrlein, slow away from the line, had an excursion across the infield after a clash with António Félix da Costa and finished 13th.

chapters.title: Auer's spin brings the field together
text: Green kept the lead through the mandatory stops and pulled away in the second half of the race. Behind him Scheider, who had stopped later than Molina, caught the Spaniard, with Mortara closing up on both, and the two swapped places at Turn 1 on lap 26, yet Molina was still ahead of the Phoenix Audi at the flag. At half distance Green was 1.7 seconds ahead of Ekström, and by the time Lucas Auer's Mercedes spun into the gravel at the end of the back straight with roughly ten minutes left, the gap was 3.5 seconds, and the safety car was deployed.

The neutralisation wiped out that cushion, and when the race was released again with five minutes to run Green complained that the safety car had been driving too slowly. 'I've had so many safety cars when I'm in the lead - it's a joke!' he said. Late on, Spengler touched Adrien Tambay's Audi and spun it around, costing the Frenchman tenth place; Tambay was classified 20th, four laps down. Spengler was penalised and Rockenfeller moved up into the final points place.

chapters.title: Green holds Ekström to 2.1 seconds
text: Green managed the restart perfectly and stayed ahead of Ekström, who was given DRS only for the last two laps, by which time Green had enough of a gap. Green took the flag after 46 laps in 1h02m33.014s, 2.144 seconds ahead, and also set the fastest lap of the race, on lap 5. It was his second win of the weekend, his third in four races and the first double of 2015.

Molina kept third, 5.038 seconds behind, ahead of Scheider, 5.678 seconds, and Mortara, 7.708 seconds, so Audi took the top five. Juncadella's Mercedes was sixth, 9.165 seconds back, after he tried to pass Mortara around the outside of Turn 1 on the final lap and could not make it stick. Christian Vietoris was seventh for Mercedes and Martin eighth for BMW, again the only BMW to score, with Müller ninth and Rockenfeller tenth. Ekström said he had not seen such dominance in his 15 years in the DTM.

chapters.title: A perfect start for Audi, questions for BMW and Mercedes
text: Green left the Lausitzring with 75 points, 17 clear of Ekström and Mortara, who were tied on 58, while Wehrlein, the best driver from outside Audi, sat fourth on 32 and Molina climbed to fifth on 27. Green had won three of the four races this year, taken pole on Sunday, and set the fastest lap in both races. He called it probably the best weekend of his career and said the Audi RS 5 DTM suited his driving style. Mortara noted that he had finished in the top five in all four races and that 14 were still to come, and Molina, who took a pole and a podium, called it his first strong weekend at the circuit.

Audi's weekend was remarkable by any measure: it had won every race of the season, held pole in every qualifying session and put seven of its eight cars in the top ten on Sunday. In the manufacturers' standings Audi had 265 points to Mercedes' 91 and BMW's 48. Gass called it the crowning of a perfect weekend but warned that the order can change quickly in the DTM, and added that the heavier cars Audi would carry at the Norisring would make the next round a difficult one.

For BMW and Mercedes the weekend raised hard questions about the Hankook tyres. Marquardt said BMW could not extract the best from the tyre over a full race distance and had needed two or three laps to get them working after the safety-car restart, and Glock suggested that winning a race in 2015 could be difficult. Mercedes team boss Ulrich Fritz said the gap to Audi was a world apart and that his cars had unexpected tyre trouble. The planned Tuesday and Wednesday test at the Lausitzring was postponed by agreement between the manufacturers, the DMSB and the ITR, and Hankook was asked for a detailed analysis.
The DTM's next round is at the Norisring in Nuremberg on 26-28 June, Audi's home event, where extra ballast will work against Green and the other Audi drivers.

facts.v: Green won both Lausitzring races, set the fastest lap in each, and has three wins from the first four races of 2015.
